description:
The configured `coordination.stale_threshold_secs` has no effect. Claim staleness always uses a hardcoded one-hour threshold, so indefinite leases go stale at a time the repository did not configure.

## Background

Configuration resolves `stale_threshold_secs` across the repository, user and system layers (`crates/jit/src/config.rs:2042-2047`), and config commands display the value. The claims coordinator never reads it:

- `crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs:1332` rebuilds the claims index with `let stale_threshold_secs = 3600u64`. It computes each indefinite lease's `stale` flag from that value and stores the value in the index.
- `crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs:210` writes the same literal into the empty index returned when no index file exists.
- `ClaimsIndex::is_stale` (`crates/jit/src/storage/claim_coordinator.rs:261`) compares against the threshold stored in the index. Lease enforcement (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:3289`) and template lease warnings (`crates/jit/src/commands/template.rs:308`) stop counting an indefinite lease as active once it is stale.

`docs/reference/configuration.md:566` says the key is accepted but does not alter claim timing.

Reproduction in a fresh git repository:

1. Add `[coordination]` with `stale_threshold_secs = 60` to `.jit/config.toml`.
2. Create an issue and acquire an indefinite claim on it (`--ttl 0 --reason probe`).
3. The JSON config output reports `"stale_threshold_secs": 60`, while `.git/jit/claims.index.json` records `"stale_threshold_secs": 3600`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The claims index, both when rebuilt and when no index file exists yet, records the effective configured `stale_threshold_secs`. It falls back to the built-in default only when no configuration layer sets the key.
- [hard] REQ-02: With a configured threshold other than the default, an indefinite lease whose last heartbeat is older than the threshold is reported stale and no longer satisfies lease enforcement, and one with a newer heartbeat does.
- [hard] REQ-03: The default stale threshold is defined in one place, and the claims coordinator and configuration both use it.
- [hard] REQ-04: The configuration reference states that `stale_threshold_secs` sets when an indefinite lease becomes stale.
- [hard] REQ-05: A regression test fails on the current code. It configures a non-default threshold and asserts both that the index records it and that a lease's staleness follows it.

## Notes

`default_ttl_secs` and `lease_renewal_threshold_pct` are displayed but also not applied. They are out of scope here. The index stores the threshold when it is built, so a threshold changed in configuration applies from the next index rebuild.
title: Honour the configured stale threshold for indefinite claim leases
